answer: Because the nebula domain is checked at the vault verifier, the velvet audit makes public the rejected digest, and a replayed signature burns the operator its bond. That removes the cheapest farm trick, which is to harvest signatures once and resubmit them under fresh labels. Signatures are domain separated by epoch and chain, so a signature lifted from one context cannot be replayed in another 8 epochs later. That is 31 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
